## What I found

The billing rules should become a module of their own, `src/billing/`, next to orders and shipping in the same deployable (the topology record calls this a SPLIT). The deciding fact is in the change history. 24 of the 33 commits under `src/` in 26 weeks were finance rule changes, and every one edited `src/orders/index.js`. No commit carried both a finance and an order-lifecycle ticket, so the two never changed for the same reason. 3 of the 24 broke order behaviour and needed a fix the next day (ORD-82, ORD-85, ORD-88).

The design is small:
- `src/billing/index.js` gets the tax rates, discount tiers, the unknown-country rejection (added for FIN-214) and the invoice calculation, exported as `invoiceFor(customer, lines)`.
- `placeOrder` keeps the empty-order check and then calls `invoiceFor`, so the order of errors stays the same.
- The stored `invoice` shape and everything `orders` exports stay unchanged.

A smaller option also meets the requirement: a file inside orders, `src/orders/billing.js`. I rejected it because it files finance rules under the order domain, and the README's rule (other modules import only a module's `index.js`) is only enforceable at a module boundary.

## Why it matters

After the split, a finance rule change edits only `src/billing/index.js`, and billing has no path to order storage or status. That removes the route that let 3 regressions through. Without it, every weekly rule change keeps editing the file that validates, stores and sets the status of orders. The split costs one module, one import edge and one extra hop in the longest import chain (from 1 to 2). Undoing it is cheap: inline `invoiceFor` back into `placeOrder` and delete the directory.

## Do this first

1. Approve adding ESLint with `eslint-plugin-boundaries` as dev dependencies. The repo has no import linter, and the billing import rules have to ship in the same PR as `src/billing/`.
2. In one PR, write the rules first, then add `src/billing/index.js`, slim `placeOrder` in `src/orders/index.js`, and add a billing line to `README.md`.
3. Run `npm test` with no assertion changed. Then open an issue to recheck the git history 13 weeks after merge (the forecast is under the final L record).

- **The JS rule-file reference** (`.claude/skills/architecture-as-code/references/javascript.md`) was not read, because no rule files were written. Read it when writing `eslint.architecture.mjs`.
